findings.claim: fa_memo.dividend_safety: "3.75% yield on a 35.24% payout, with per-share dividend rising from Rs8.0 (2025) to Rs9.0 (2026)"
findings.issue: Internal inconsistency in the dossier's own fundamental block: payout_ratio (35.24%) implies an EPS basis of ~Rs25.54 (9.0 / 0.3524), but the same fundamental block's eps field (also used for the P/E, forward P/E, and all four valuation methods) is Rs22.64. Using the stated EPS of 22.64, the true payout on the latest Rs9.0 dividend is 9.0/22.64 = 39.7%, not 35.24% — a ~4.5pp / ~13% gap between two figures in the same record. The room text repeats both numbers verbatim without flagging the mismatch, so the dividend-safety read is built on two different EPS bases at once.
findings.fix: Reconcile the EPS basis used for payout_ratio against the eps field (22.64) in the fundamentals pipeline; either correct payout_ratio to ~39.7% (consistent with eps=22.64 and the Rs9.0 dividend) or document that payout_ratio uses a different (e.g. full-year/consolidated) EPS than the eps field feeding P/E and valuation — and have fa_memo note the wider, ~40% payout range rather than the single 35.24% figure until reconciled.

summary: HCAR's headline numbers check out: composite_fair (228.71) is exactly the median of the four valuation methods, mispricing_pct (-3.0%) is arithmetically correct, price_at_session/RSI/SMA readings match the dossier and correctly describe a downtrend (price below SMA20 242.25 and SMA50 244.98, RSI14 43.3), the ta_memo's directional claim is internally consistent with the stated structure (unlike some other tickers' sessions), there is no broker claim in play to audit, no advice-language leaks, and the 39% FY26 Pakistan car-sales figure cited as a bull pillar is independently confirmed by Business Recorder. One real but non-fatal defect: the dossier's payout_ratio (35.24%) doesn't reconcile with its own EPS field (22.64) against the latest Rs9.0 dividend, a data-layer inconsistency the memo repeats without flagging.
